summary:
Dr. Md. Rajibul Islam is a distinguished researcher and academic with a strong interdisciplinary background in computer applications and photonics engineering. He earned his Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA) from Indira Gandhi National Open University, New Delhi, India, in 2004, followed by a Master of Science in Information Technology (Biometric Image Processing) from Multimedia University, Malaysia, in 2010.

Dr. Islam began his professional journey as a Research Assistant and Software Engineer at various university research institutes and R&D divisions within Malaysian software firms. In 2014, he returned to academia to pursue a Ph.D. in Physics (Photonics Engineering) at the Photonics Research Centre, University of Malaya, which he completed in 2017.

He recently completed a research fellowship at the Photonics Research Institute of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University and has since returned to his position as an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT).

Earlier in his academic career, Dr. Islam also served as an Assistant Professor and Head of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Asia Pacific (UAP). He was a Visiting Ph.D. Researcher at the University of Limerick, Ireland, through the Erasmus Mundus – INTACT scholarship program.

His research interests span machine learning, artificial intelligence, data mining, optical fiber sensors, and photonic devices. With approximately 100 peer-reviewed scientific publications, as well as several books and book chapters, Dr. Islam is a highly active contributor to the global scientific community. He also serves as a reviewer for numerous international journals and participates regularly in the scientific committees of international conferences.

summary:
Professor Ali is a Professor in the Department of Data Science and Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences, and the Vice Chancellor of Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He also serves as an Adjunct Professor at the School of Science, Computing and Engineering Technologies, Swinburne University of Technology, Australia.

From 1997 to 2024, he held academic positions from Lecturer to Professor at universities across Australia, Asia, and the South Pacific in Computer Science and Information Systems, and worked as an AI expert in Australia and Fiji. After earning his PhD in Machine Learning from Monash University in 2005, he served in leadership roles including Programme and Research Coordinator, Head of Department, Director of Research Center, Dean, and Acting Vice Chancellor. He chaired committees on programme development, ICT, recruitment, evaluation, and accreditation, and was General Chair of international conferences. He has supervised over 20 postgraduate students.

He holds an h-index of 35 (Google Scholar), has authored two books, edited six, and published 150+ refereed journal and conference papers on Machine Learning, including SVM, Neural Networks, Deep Learning, and Ensemble Learning. He established two international conferences and served as Chief Editor of international journals. He secured research grants exceeding 7 million from industry, government, and international bodies such as the EU, USAID, the World Bank, Canadian agencies, and Australian industries.

His awards include the Bangladesh Expatriates’ Award 2023 (Research and Innovation), Vice-Chancellor Research Excellence Award 2014, Outstanding Leadership Award 2013, and others. He is a Senior Member of Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE).

Dr. Muhammad Aminur Rahaman, SMIEEE, is an Associate Professor in the Department of Data Science and Engineering at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT), where he also serves as the Dean of the Faculty of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, and CITO. Dr. Rahaman earned his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) from Islamic University, Kustia, Bangladesh. Subsequently, he obtained a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Dhaka, under a fully funded scholarship from the ICT Ministry of Bangladesh. His research interests include AI and machine learning, computer vision, image processing, medical imaging, Bangla NLP, HCI, robotics, and software engineering. He has published extensively in high-impact, Q1, SCIE-indexed, and Scopus-indexed journals, as well as at IEEE conferences. He has secured and led numerous funded research grants and has received multiple prestigious awards, including Research Excellence and Outstanding Research awards. 

Dr. Rahaman has played key roles in OBE-based curriculum development for emerging programs in CSE, AI and data science, robotics, cybersecurity, and software engineering. As a Senior Member of IEEE and an active leader within the IEEE Computer Society Bangladesh Chapter, he has served in numerous national and international conference leadership roles, editorial boards, and peer-review panels, and has been repeatedly recognized for excellence in student mentorship and professional service.

Mr. Hossain is committed to continuous professional development, interdisciplinary research, and student-centered teaching, with the long-term goal of contributing to impactful research and quality higher education in computer science and engineering.

Prof. Dr. Ahmed Al Mansur is an accomplished academic and researcher currently serving as a Professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). With over 15 years of experience in academia and research, he has established himself as a prominent figure in Renewable Energy Systems, particularly in photovoltaic (PV) array optimization and performance analysis.

Dr. Mansur holds a Ph.D. in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from the Islamic University of Technology (IUT), where he achieved a perfect 4.0 CGPA. His extensive administrative leadership includes roles as the Director of the Centre for Research Innovation and Transformation (CRIT) and the Center for International Affairs at Green University of Bangladesh (GUB). He is recognized as an IEEE Senior Member (SMIEEE). He has actively contributed to the professional community as a TPC Co-Chair for the STI Conference 2025 and an Educational Activities Coordinator for the IEEE PES SC-Bangladesh Section.

As a prolific researcher, Dr. Mansur has secured numerous government-funded and international research grants from organizations such as the ICT Division and the Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST). His research has led to the development of a patented Indoor Testing System for Solar PV modules and to significant contributions to the literature, with numerous publications in high-impact journals such as Energy Reports, Sustainability, and Energies. He has been honored with multiple awards, including Silver Medals at the Research Innovation Commercialization & Entrepreneurship Showcase (RICES) 2021 and several Research Excellence Awards for his contributions to sustainable energy management. His expertise encompasses Power Electronics, Optimization Algorithms, and the development of specialized laboratory facilities for renewable energy research.

summary: Mr. Mohammad Jahidul Islam obtained both his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Physics from Jagannath University, obtaining 4th position in his B.Sc. studies and 2nd position in his M.Sc. studies. Currently, he is working as an assistant professor in the Department of EEE at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). Moreover, he is also working as an assistant proctor at BUBT. At BUBT, he teaches undergraduate-level Physics, Electronic Properties of Materials, and Engineering Electromagnetics. His teaching approach emphasizes clear concepts, analytical skills, and real-world applications of engineering with high regard for OBE. He encourages his students through the process of critical thinking and problem-solving. His areas of research interest are materials science, computational physics, and crystallography. He specifically enjoys designing transition metal-based semiconductor and superconducting materials and studying their various properties, including structural, electronic, elastic, thermodynamic, thermoelectric, mechanical, and optical properties, using Density Functional Theory (DFT) with CASTEP, Material Studio, and Gaussian software. He is also active in IEEE student development activities, guiding technical groups and organizing academic seminars and workshops.

summary:
Ruhul Amin is a Lecturer in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT), Dhaka, where he has been serving since 2022. He is an early-career academic and researcher in electrical engineering and an active research profile in optics and photonics.
He completed his B.Sc. in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST), Bangladesh. His academic background in electronics, circuits, and communication systems led to a focused research interest in optics and photonics. His primary research areas include fiber-optic sensors, optical fiber communication, supercontinuum generation, surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensors, nonlinear optics, and nanophotonic device design.
Mr. Amin has published several research articles in reputed international journals, including IEEE Photonics, IEEE Sensors Journal, Physica Scripta, IEEE Transactions on NanoBioscience, Ceramics International, Optical and Quantum Electronics, and Alexandria Engineering Journal. His work emphasizes the design of novel photonic crystal fiber structures with ultra-high birefringence, enhanced nonlinearity, and improved sensing efficiency for applications in optical communication, biosensing, and lab-on-chip technologies.
At BUBT, he teaches EEE 101 – Electrical Technology, EEE 102 – Electrical Technology Lab, EEE 303 – Digital Electronics, EEE 304 – Digital Electronics Lab, and EEE 329 – VLSI Circuits I. He is also actively involved in Outcome-Based Education (OBE) implementation and the SDG Committee for Impact Rankings. 
His long-term goal is to contribute to advanced research in nanophotonics, fiber-optic sensors, and nonlinear optical devices while continuing to mentor and inspire future engineers.

summary: Mahmudur Rahman is a Lecturer in the Department of Civil Engineering at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He has completed his M.Sc. in Geotechnical Engineering from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), with a research focus on Landslide Susceptibility Analysis and natural hazard mitigation. His research interests encompass slope stability analysis, landslide susceptibility assessment, rainfall–soil interaction, soil health monitoring, ground improvement techniques, and the characterization of soil behavior under varying environmental and geotechnical conditions. His research integrates field investigations, laboratory testing, GIS-based studies, solid waste management, soft soil improvement, and numerical modeling to advance sustainable solutions for geotechnical hazards. Mr. Rahman is a recipient of the prestigious National Science and Technology (NST) Fellowship awarded by the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of Bangladesh. He has actively contributed to several research initiatives, including institutionally funded projects at BUBT, and has published research in peer-reviewed journals and international conference proceedings. His technical expertise includes geotechnical analysis and structural modeling using GeoStudio, GIS, ETABS, AutoCAD, and other engineering software. Through his teaching, research, and professional engagement, he is committed to advancing resilient infrastructure, sustainable geotechnical engineering practices, and innovative solutions to contemporary civil engineering challenges.

summary:
Md. Tanzil Hawlader is a Lecturer in the Department of Civil Engineering at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT) and a postgraduate student in Civil and Structural Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). He completed his Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Civil Engineering from BUET with a major in Structural Engineering and is currently pursuing his Master of Science (MSc) in Civil and Structural Engineering.

He has professional experience as a Junior Engineer and has been actively involved in a wide range of structural engineering projects conducted under BUET–BRTC. His notable professional works include structural analysis and assessment of reinforced concrete and steel buildings, design evaluation of steel structures for stadium facilities, assessment and retrofitting of existing multi-storied residential and commercial buildings, foundation design and adequacy checking for shallow and deep foundations, and structural design vetting of academic and institutional buildings. His responsibilities covered numerical modeling, hand calculations, structural safety evaluation, and preparation of technical assessment reports in compliance with BNBC and relevant international standards.

His academic and research interests include structural engineering, composite structures, steel structures, reinforced concrete design, foundation engineering, earthquake engineering, and sustainable construction materials such as recycled aggregate and fiber-reinforced concrete. His academic work reflects a strong integration of code-based design principles with practical engineering applications.

Md. Tanzil Hawlader aims to contribute to research-led teaching and professional practice by bridging advanced structural research with real-world engineering solutions for safe, resilient, and sustainable infrastructure.

summary:
Mohammad Mahmudur Rahman Khan is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Textile Engineering at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He joined BUBT in October 2012 as a Lecturer and was promoted to Assistant Professor in January 2016. With over a decade of experience in higher education, he has been actively involved in teaching, curriculum delivery, academic coordination, and student mentoring in the B.Sc. in Textile Engineering program.

Mr. Khan completed his B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). His research interests include noise and vibration, thermal and fluid engineering, and machine learning, with a growing focus on interdisciplinary and sustainability-oriented engineering applications. He is a co-author of a Springer Nature book chapter titled “Green Coloration Process Targeting Sustainability,” which contributes to the discourse on environmentally responsible textile processing and sustainable manufacturing practices.

He teaches a broad range of core and applied engineering courses, including Fundamentals of Mechanical Engineering, Automation and Robotics in Textiles, Fundamentals of Machine Dynamics and Machine Design, Engineering Drawing, Maintenance of Textile Machines, and Workshop Practice. A strong proponent of Outcomes-Based Education (OBE), Mr. Khan actively contributes to the implementation of OBE across departmental courses, emphasizing continuous improvement, practical skills, and industry relevance.

Through his commitment to quality teaching, interdisciplinary research, and sustainable engineering education, Mr. Khan continues to contribute meaningfully to the academic and professional development of textile engineering graduates at BUBT.

summary:

My professional journey began with an internship at Echotex Ltd from October to November 2015, where I gained practical exposure to textile manufacturing operations and industrial processes.

Driven by a passion for education and research, I transitioned into academia by joining Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT) on October 8, 2016, as a Lecturer in the Department of Textile Engineering. Through dedication to teaching, student mentoring, and academic development, I was promoted to Assistant Professor in August 2022.

Alongside teaching, I have actively contributed to research in textile engineering and related fields. To date, I have published nine research articles in reputed international journals, receiving approximately 400 citations, reflecting the impact and recognition of my scholarly work. I have also presented two conference papers at renowned international conferences, demonstrating continued engagement with the global academic and research community.

Mohammad Saifuddin is a dedicated Assistant Professor of Statistics at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT), a position he has held since July 2022. With a career in academia spanning over a decade, including previous roles as a Lecturer at BUBT and Bangladesh University, he has developed a deep expertise in delivering complex statistical curricula and mentoring students. (Hons.) in Applied Statistics from the Institute of Statistical Research & Training (ISRT) at the University of Dhaka, where he earned First Class honors for both degrees and received the ISRT Merit Scholarship.

Saifuddin’s research profile is characterized by a strong focus on Design of Experiment (DoE), Response Surface Methodology (RSM), and Multivariate Analysis. His work frequently bridges the gap between theoretical statistics and practical applications, as evidenced by his publications on optimization in pharmaceutical formulations, time series forecasting for aquaculture, and mathematical modeling of co-infection dynamics. He is highly proficient in advanced data analytics, utilizing a technical toolkit that includes R, Python, and SQL, alongside specialized software like SPSS and Minitab.

In addition to his teaching and research, Saifuddin has demonstrated a commitment to continuous professional development, recently completing a Machine Learning Specialization through DeepLearning.AI in October 2025. His global communication skills are further validated by an IELTS overall band score of 6.5. Through his diverse publication record and his role as a researcher, he continues to contribute significantly to fields ranging from economic development to health science and industrial optimization.

summary: Md. Reza Hassan Khan, currently serving as an Assistant Professor and Acting Head of the Department of English, is an academician and dedicated educator with fifteen years of experience at the Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). His academic journey began at Jahangirnagar University (JU), where he earned his BA (Hons) and MA in English, providing him with a rigorous foundation in both literary and linguistic studies. He is currently advancing his scholarly profile as a doctoral researcher at the Centre for Higher Studies and Research (CHSR). His research and academic interests are deeply rooted in Critical Literary and Cultural Theory, with a specific focus on the intersections of Trauma Studies and Masculinity. His work often utilizes psychoanalytic lenses to explore the complexities of the human condition, particularly within the realm of American Literature. Furthermore, his scholarly inquiry extends into Gender Studies and the psychosocial frameworks of modern and contemporary narratives. As an educator, he has consistently engaged with students at both the BA and MA levels and has successfully supervised numerous undergraduate research projects, fostering a culture of critical inquiry among his pupils. Beyond the classroom, his role as HoD involves navigating the complexities of institutional quality assurance and curriculum development, ensuring that the department remains a hub for academic excellence and ethical professional practice.

summary:
Prof Dr K Ahmed Alam has a 23-year career of teaching, academic administration, and research
at the university level. Currently, he is Professor in the Department of English, Dean, Faculty of
Arts, Humanities and Social Science, and Director, Institutional Quality Assurance Cell
(IQAC) at Bangladesh University of Business and technology (BUBT). Formerly, he was
Professor of English, Dean in the Faculty of Science and Humanities, and Director of
Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) at Bangladesh Army International University of
Science and Technology (BAIUST), Cumilla. Before that, he had been Associate Professor and
Head/ Chairperson in the Department of English at reputed private universities. He did his PhD
in the Department of English, Jahangirnagar University. His areas of interest include Writing,
Pedagogy, Postcolonial/ Commonwealth Literature, Dalit Literature, Critical Theory, Cultural
Studies, and Translation Studies. He has published a good number of articles in local and
international research journals. He has already participated in numerous international
conferences. His published book, Anubadbidya: Itihas O Tattwa (Translation Studies: History
and Theory), attracts the attention of the students and academics of the country. He has recently
published a book of Bamgla poems, titled Nakkhotromanobi O Kotipoy Ponktimala (A Celestial
Woman and Some Verses). He has also completed a manuscript—A Handbook for Theory
Beginners. Very often, he writes in esteemed Weeklies and Dailies on literature, literary theory,
and contemporary issues. Besides, he is an OBE curriculum developer and a Trainer for Quality
Assurance, Pedagogy, OBE Curriculum Development, Assessment, and Preparedness for
Attaining Accreditation.

summary:
Mohamad Shawkat Ali is an Associate Professor of English at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He teaches courses in English Language, Linguistics, English Language Teaching (ELT), and Literature at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels. He has been teaching in higher education since 1998 and has extensive experience in academic writing, classroom-based instruction, curriculum development, and research supervision.

He holds a BA (Hons) and an MA in English Literature from the University of Dhaka, and an MA in International English Language Teaching and Applied Language Studies from London Metropolitan University, UK. His academic interests include ELT, applied linguistics, academic writing, error analysis, sociolinguistics, and pedagogy in higher education.

His research focuses on classroom-based ELT research, learner errors in writing, and the sociocultural dimensions of English language use in Bangladesh. He has published seven research articles in reputable journals and has translated a number of scholarly articles and books. He remains actively engaged in academic research, mentoring, and professional development in English language education.

summary:
Md. Shirazur Rahman is an Assistant Professor in the Department of English at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT), with more than 11 years of experience in higher education teaching, academic research, and institutional responsibilities. He has been teaching as an Assistant Professor since November 2018, after previously working as a Lecturer and Teaching Assistant in the same department. 

Mr. Rahman completed his M.A. in English Language Teaching (ELT) and B.A. (Honours) in English from BUBT with good results. He is currently pursuing a PhD in Applied Linguistics at the English Discipline, School of Arts and Humanities, Khulna University. His academic interests include Linguistic Politeness, Pragmatics, Sociolinguistics, English Language Teaching (ELT) & applied linguistics, language assessment, motivation in language learning, and sociolinguistic influences on language use. He has published a number of research articles in recognized peer reviewed academic journals. He has also been actively involved in academic publishing as an Editorial Assistant of the BUBT Journal since 2014.

In addition to teaching and research, Mr. Rahman played a significant role in the establishment and operation of the BUBT Language Lab under the HEQEP project funded by the World Bank and UGC, serving as a member of the SPM team and later on as Deputy Sub Project Manager. He has participated in numerous professional trainings and workshops on research methodology, outcome-based education, quality assurance, language lab teaching, and academic ethics. Committed to quality education and continuous professional development, he actively contributes to teaching innovation and academic excellence at BUBT.

summary:
S. M. Mostasim Billah is a Lecturer in English at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He holds a Bachelor’s degree in English and a Master’s degree in Applied Linguistics and ELT from the University of Dhaka. His academic training and professional experience reflect a strong grounding in language pedagogy, curriculum design, and assessment at both secondary and tertiary levels. Although his specialization lies in Applied Linguistics and ELT, his teaching expertise also encompasses English Literature, reflecting a balanced academic profile in both language and literary studies.

He has taught courses such as Introduction to Semantics and Pragmatics, English Language, and 18th Century English Literature, demonstrating competence in linguistic theory, language skills development, and literary analysis. His teaching philosophy emphasizes concept-based learning, critical thinking, and communicative competence rather than rote memorization. He regularly designs learner-centered instructional materials and writing tasks appropriate for intermediate and undergraduate learners.

He previously served as a Teacher at St. Joseph Higher Secondary School, where his responsibilities included conducting classes, setting examination questions, evaluating answer scripts, and performing other institutional duties. During his student life, he also worked as a student mentor, providing academic and psychological support to junior students, which helped lay the foundation for his professional teaching practice.

His research interests include grammar instruction in EFL contexts, storytelling as a pedagogical tool, discourse analysis, pragmatic competence, and literature-informed language teaching. He aspires to pursue higher studies in ELT and contribute to research-driven English education at both national and international levels.

summary:
Md. Mahmudul Hassan, Ph.D. is a Professor and Chairman in the Department of Economics at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT). He earned his Doctor of Philosophy in Economics from Jahangirnagar University in 2019. Earlier, he completed his M.Sc. in Economics and B.Sc. in Economics at the same university, building a strong academic foundation in economics. His Ph.D. work covered analyzing efficiency of poultry farms in Bangladesh which is mainly a branch of Agricultural Economics. 
Mr. Hassan then joined BUBT as a Lecturer, progressed to Assistant Professor, and served as Associate Professor. Since 1 January 2026, he has been serving as Professor. With more than 15 years of academic experience, he has developed a strong record of teaching, research, and scholarly engagement. He has a significant number of scholarly publications in domestic (such as Bangladesh Development Studies) and international journals. 
Professionally, he has served as a Trainer at the National Academy for Development for entry-level BCS (Administration) Cadre Officers, including the “5th Development Administration” training session. He is a member of the Bangladesh Economic Association and has supported student engagement through the BUBT Economics Club as Moderator and later Chief Moderator since July 2025. His commitment to research strengthens his teaching and drives his interest in fiscal policy and institutional development.
